title: Stale worktrees: 51 of them, 24 GB, being pruned safely

chat.text: 47 of 51 worktrees are fully merged into michael/dev. An Opus task mastermind runs the existing prune script, salvage-commits any leftover changes onto each worktree's own branch before removing it (nothing deleted from git), and decides where worktrees should live and why they piled up.

message.text: Taken: clean up the 51 worktrees, no data lost. I'm doing it alone, with no minions: dry run first, then prune what is clean, then commit the leftovers to each worktree's own branch before removing it.

✅ Worktrees went from 33.3 GB to 6.0 GB and nothing was lost. 28 merged worktrees were pruned. 14 others had leftover changes, so I committed those on each one's own branch first ([manifest](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/mastermind-repo-slim/worktree-cleanup/manifest.json)). I also removed 24 half-deleted folders whose files are all in git. 8 stay on purpose: 4 pool slots, the locked qf-5, and 3 unmerged branches for you to look at (orphans, readmeaudit, refine-demo).

Decisions ([worktrees.md](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/mastermind-repo-slim/worktree-cleanup/doc/worktrees.md)):
- Worktrees move to C:/Code/lew42/workspace/worktrees/. API keys stay in %LOCALAPPDATA%\lew42\servex, where Servex already reads them.
- Quick-fix worktrees weren't being reused for two reasons. The skills send every multi-file task to a fresh worktree. And the pool's cleanup was stuck for 24 h on a stale lock in qf-1, which left 150 duplicate salvage branches; I unblocked it.
- The one fix for the pile-up: Servex's 10-minute sweep runs worktree-prune.mjs --salvage --idle-hours 6. The script side is built; hooking it into the sweep is a Servex follow-up.

Full [report](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/mastermind-repo-slim/worktree-cleanup/report.md).
